Two goals apiece from Thierry Henry and Lionel Messi, alongside headers from Carles Puyol and Gerard Piqué, swept aside Juande Ramos’s team and effectively sealed the La Liga title for the Catalans. The victory moves Barcelona four points clear at the top of the table with just four games remaining, ending Madrid’s 18-game unbeaten run and devastating their hopes of a late title surge.

The match began with Real Madrid looking to capitalize on their home advantage. In the 14th minute, Sergio Ramos burst down the right wing and delivered a precise cross for Gonzalo Higuaín, who unmarked, headed past Víctor Valdés to send the Bernabéu into raptures. 

However, Madrid’s lead lasted less than four minutes as Guardiola’s tactical masterstroke began to unfold. Deploying Lionel Messi in a revolutionary "false nine" central role, Barcelona overwhelmed Madrid’s midfield pivot of Lassana Diarra and Fernando Gago. 

In the 18th minute, Messi floated a subtle pass over the head of Cannavaro, allowing Thierry Henry to calmly cushion the ball and slot it past Iker Casillas for the equalizer. Just two minutes later, Barcelona took the lead. Xavi Hernandez whipped in a pin-point free-kick, and captain Carles Puyol rose highest to power a header into the net before famously tearing off his captain's armband to kiss it in front of the traveling contingent.

Barcelona’s suffocating press produced a third goal ten minutes before the break. Xavi caught Diarra in possession deep in Madrid's half and quickly set up Messi, who coolly slotted the ball low past Casillas to make it 3-1.

Real Madrid offered a brief glimmer of hope ten minutes after the restart. Arjen Robben curled in a dangerous free-kick, allowing Sergio Ramos to head home and pull the hosts back to 3-2. 

Yet, any hopes of a Madrid comeback were crushed almost immediately. Barely two minutes later, Xavi carved open the host's defense with a sublime long pass, sending Henry sprinting clear of the offside trap to slide the ball past an advancing Casillas for his second of the night.

From there, Barcelona turned the match into a masterclass. In the 75th minute, a brilliant team move ended with Xavi turning in the box and rolling the ball to Messi, who beat Casillas at his near post for 5-2. The humiliation was completed seven minutes from time when defender Gerard Piqué surged forward, picked up Samuel Eto’o’s low cross, turned, and squeezed the ball inside the post to score Barca's sixth, celebrating by stretching out his jersey in triumph.

The victory marks the first time Barcelona have scored six goals at the Santiago Bernabéu and stands as a terrifying statement of intent to the rest of Europe. 

**Eyes on Stamford Bridge**

With La Liga now firmly within their grasp, Barcelona must quickly turn their attention to Europe. Guardiola’s side travels to London this Wednesday for the second leg of their UEFA Champions League semi-final against Chelsea. 

Following a grueling 0-0 draw in the first leg at the Camp Nou last week, Barcelona face a daunting test at Stamford Bridge. However, buoyed by tonight's six-goal spectacle—and despite looming suspension issues for Puyol and an injury worry for Rafael Márquez—the Blaugrana will head to England full of belief that a historic treble remains well within their reach.
